web_evidence.source: Drinking Alcohol with COVID-19: Tips for Use, Safety, Risks
web_evidence.title: Drinking Alcohol with COVID-19: Tips for Use, Safety, Risks
web_evidence.content:
There’s a pervasive myth that alcohol prevents COVID-19. While hand sanitizer containing alcohol may kill the virus on surfaces, drinking alcohol doesn’t cure or prevent a COVID-19 infection.

Alcohol consumption may make your symptoms worse, according to the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA).

Alcohol can also weaken your immune system and contribute to risk-taking behavior (like not wearing a mask) that could increase your chances of contracting the virus.

web_evidence.title: Covid and Alcohol: Can You Drink Alcohol with Covid - The Cabin Rehab Thailand
web_evidence.content: No, alcohol does not kill coronavirus inside the body, though it can destroy the virus on surfaces when used at concentrations of 60 percent or higher. Alcohol-based disinfectants work by breaking down the virus’s lipid layer when applied directly to contaminated surfaces. Internal consumption remains ineffective, as the coronavirus replicates inside cells where alcohol in the bloodstream cannot neutralize viral particles. Drinking alcohol during an infection causes harm by suppressing immune [...] No, drinking alcohol does not kill COVID or help fight the virus. The belief that alcohol cures infection is a myth, as alcohol consumed internally does not eliminate viral particles or enhance immune defense. Alcohol disinfects surfaces through direct contact, yet ingestion does not produce the same effect within the body. Viral load remains unchanged with alcohol intake, as the virus replicates inside cells and is unaffected by alcohol circulating in the bloodstream. Alcohol weakens the [...] suppressing immune function, increasing dehydration, and worsening symptoms such as fever and fatigue. Belief in the myth that alcohol cures coronavirus introduces serious risks, including delayed medical care, increased infection severity, and long-term harm from alcohol misuse. Clear distinction between surface disinfection and internal use prevents misinformation and supports safer health decisions during outbreaks.

who_evidence.source: [PDF] Alcohol and COVID-19: what you need to know - EMRO
who_evidence.title: [PDF] Alcohol and COVID-19: what you need to know - EMRO
who_evidence.content:
1 Under no circumstances should you drink any type of alcoholic product as a means of preventing or treating COVID-19 infection Consumption of alcohol will not protect you from COVID-19 Alcohol is a harmful substance that has an adverse effect on almost every single organ of your body, and the risk of damage to your health increases with each drink consumed. Alcohol use, especially heavy use, weakens the immune system and reduces its ability to cope with infectious diseases, including COVID-19. [...] Drinking strong alcohol kills the virus in the inhaled air.
Consumption of alcohol will not kill the virus in the inhaled air; it will not disinfect your mouth and throat; and it will not give you any kind of protection against COVID-19.
Alcohol (beer, wine, distilled spirits or herbal alcohol) stimulates immunity and resistance to the virus.
Alcohol has a deleterious effect on your immune system and will not stimulate immunity and virus resistance. [...] Alcohol and COVID-19: what you need to know General myths about alcohol and COVID-19 Consuming alcohol destroys the virus that causes COVID-19.
Consuming alcohol will not destroy the virus, and its consump­ tion is likely to increase the health risks if a person becomes infected with the virus. Alcohol (at a concentration of at least 60% by volume) works as a disinfectant on your skin, but it has no such effect within your system when ingested.

who_evidence.title: Alcohol does not protect against COVID-19; access should be restricted during lockdown
who_evidence.content: Alcohol consumption is associated with a range of communicable and noncommunicable diseases and mental health disorders, which can make a person more vulnerable to COVID-19. In particular, alcohol compromises the body’s immune system and increases the risk of adverse health outcomes. Therefore, people should minimize their alcohol consumption at any time, and particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. [...] Fear and misinformation have generated a dangerous myth that consuming high-strength alcohol can kill the COVID-19 virus. It does not. Consuming any alcohol poses health risks, but consuming high-strength ethyl alcohol (ethanol), particularly if it has been adulterated with methanol, can result in severe health consequences, including death. [...] Alcohol is known to be harmful to health in general, and is well understood to increase the risk of injury and violence, including intimate partner violence, and can cause alcohol poisoning. At times of lockdown during the COVID-19 pandemic, alcohol consumption can exacerbate health vulnerability, risk-taking behaviours, mental health issues and violence.
